A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NMR self-difusion measurements and tape-stripping studies with (19) F-NMR quantification are valuable techniques in the development of new topical microemulsions.
(19) F is an excellent nucleus for NMR studies of fluorinated compounds in microemulsions and for monitoring skin penetration processes.
(19) F-NMR spectroscopy is an excellent method for the quantification of fluorinated drug amounts in tape-stripped skin and for the characterization of the microstructure of the microemulsions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of (19)F NMR with tape stripping is an excellent approach to investigate the penetration behavior of fluorinated compounds in skin penetration experiments.
(19) F-NMR spectroscopy is a valuable tool for the quantification of the skin penetration of fluorinated drugs from natural microemulsified formulations.
NMR is a valuable tool to monitor the skin penetration of fluorinated compounds from natural microemulsified formulations.
